newsitem.title: INDIA: India's monsoon rains seen one week late.
newsitem.headline: India's monsoon rains seen one week late.

text.p: India's monsoon rains, which normally hit the southwestern tip of the subcontinent around June 1, are likely to arrive about a week late this year, meteorological department officials said on Tuesday.
"They might hit after June 7th or 8th," a senior official at the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) told Reuters.
The monsoon rains usually start around June 1 and move progressively north, eventually covering the entire country before tapering off in September.
"The monsoon rains are getting delayed because of the influence of the middle latitude system over the Indian region," said A.V.R.K. Krishna Rao, a senior official at the IMD.
The IMD last month predicted the rains would arrive around June 1 for the 10th year in a row.
